biodiversity_overview.text: 405 GBIF occurrence records for 27 tracked species are attributed to Manipur, spanning 1867-2026.
382 of these records (94.3%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 12, Magnoliopsida 8, Mammalia 4, Actinopterygii 1, Amphibia 1, Testudines 1.

threatened_species.text: 2 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian White-eye (133), Indian Pied Starling (98), Indian Cuckoo (60), Indian Pond-heron (37), Mango (14).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 7 in 2016 to 42 in 2024. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 3.47% of Manipur's area (7 areas intersect the state).
11.3% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (43 of 382); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), East Indian Ash (0.43), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Indian Grass-babbler (0.30), Bulletwood (0.30).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Manipur (equal-weight reference): cell near 25.125N 94.125E (overall rank 165, median rank across weightings 180); cell near 24.375N 94.125E (overall rank 247, median rank across weightings 256); cell near 24.375N 93.375E (overall rank 473, median rank across weightings 463).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 18,034 km2 (77.16% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

2,687.1 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (14.9% of the 2000 extent; 9.43% in 2015-2024, rank 4 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2016 (228.46 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 0.62% of land and population density is 148.8 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
12% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.

sources: Hansen et al. Global Forest Change 2000-2024 v1.12 (CC BY 4.0)
GHSL R2023A built-up and population 2020 (CC BY 4.0)
